speaker_role: former admissions officer turned IvyWise counselor plus a second IvyWise counselor (Mike); webinar-style
commercial_incentive: IvyWise sells counseling, academic advising and a mock admissions committee service (Roundtable), promoted repeatedly.
key_insights: Speaker says the most recent cycle was among the most competitive ever, with many applicants holding perfect grades and scores, so being a strong student alone is not enough.
Selective schools read holistically, seeking curious, thoughtful people who will contribute to campus, not only academic excellence.
Intellectual curiosity is framed as the key Stanford trait; the difference between loving school and loving learning shows up through specific, enthusiastic writing.
Applicants need not declare a major when applying, and formal declaration is not due until the end of sophomore year.
Most of the video is a Stanford program tour: general education requirements, research funding, study abroad, career center, internships.
Essays are called especially important at a hyper-selective school; counselors brainstorm personal statements, then supplements once prompts release.
Getting several former admissions officers to review an application is pitched as useful because individual readers hold different values.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Stanford has 66 undergraduate majors across three of seven schools (counselor Mike).
Sponsored research budget above $2 billion and 15 independent labs, centers and institutes (Mike).
Nearly half of Stanford students study abroad (Mike).
Language requirement: one year of college-level study or proficiency testing (speaker).
Stanford accepts Common App, Coalition App and QuestBridge (Mike).
notable_or_distinctive: Mostly a university brochure-style overview with a light admissions message about intellectual curiosity.
reliability_notes: Heavily promotional for IvyWise, thin on actual admissions criteria, and program details are stated without sources and may be dated.
